question: to the Commission Benoit Cassart (Renew) Subject:

The statement in the minutes of the Council meeting on Directive 77/388/EEC of 17 May 1977 on the harmonisation of the laws of the Member States relating to turnover taxes establishes the following in the relative part of Article 4 (‘Taxable Persons’): ‘the Council and the Commission declare that Member States may consider as not liable to value added tax individuals engaged in honorary activities as well as managers, directors, [members of the supervisory board] and company liquidators in their relations with the companies to the extent that they form a part of such companies’. 1.

Does the Commission conclude, in line with that statement, that, today, a Member State is not required to consider the services provided by directors who are natural persons as falling within the scope of VAT?

If so, does the Commission consider that such directors who are natural persons may be exempted from any administrative obligations in terms of VAT in their Member State of residence, including when they hold an appointment in a company established in another Member State which does not apply this exclusion from the scope of VAT in the same way?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (16.9.2026) Under Article 9(1) of Council Directive 2006/112/EC1 (the value-added tax (VAT) Directive), any person who, independently, carries out in any place any economic activity, whatever the purpose or results of that activity, is regarded as a taxable person. Whether the activity of a company director who is a natural person falls within the scope of the VAT Directive must be assessed in the light of that provision and the relevant case-law of the European Court of Justice, in particular as regards the condition of independent economic activity. The Court has clarified that a member of the board of directors of a public limited company does not carry out an economic activity independently, within the meaning of Article 9(1) of the VAT Directive, where that person does not act on his or her own behalf or under his or her own responsibility, and does not bear the economic risk linked to the activity2. The assessment depends on the factual circumstances of the activity concerned. Where a director, as a natural person, resides in one Member State but holds a position in a company established in another Member State, the VAT treatment is assessed by the Member State where the taxation of the activity takes place according to the place of supply rules in the VAT Directive. If this Member State considers the director’s activity to be an independent taxable service, this will result in VAT obligations to occur in that Member State in connection with that supply. The director may be allowed under certain conditions to apply the small businesses VAT exemption scheme3, available since 1 January 2025, also in Member States where they are not established.
1 Council Directive 2006/112/EC of 28 November 2006 on the common system of value added tax, OJ L 347,
11.12.2006, pp. 1–118. 2 Judgment of 21 December 2023, TP v Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, C‑288/22, EU:C:2023:1024. 3 See https://sme-vat-rules.ec.europa.eu/index_en.
